title: Creamy banana porridge
summary: Smooth, slow-cooked oats with mashed banana and a little honey.
steps: Put the oats and milk in a small pan over a low heat.
Mash half the banana and stir it in.
Cook for 6–8 minutes, stirring often, until thick and very soft. Add a splash more milk if needed.
Top with the rest of the banana, sliced, plus the honey and cinnamon.
tip: Cook the oats well so they're soft. If oats bother you, use fine 'instant' oats or ready brek-style oats, which are smoother.

title: Soft scrambled eggs on toast
summary: Silky, buttery scrambled eggs on white sourdough.
steps: Beat the eggs with the milk and a pinch of salt.
Melt the butter in a non-stick pan over a low heat.
Add the eggs and stir slowly with a spatula until just set and creamy.
Toast the bread and spoon the eggs on top.
tip: White sourdough is lower in fibre than wholemeal or seeded bread, and usually has a short ingredient list.

title: Banana & peanut butter smoothie
summary: A filling, protein-rich smoothie that's easy on the gut.
steps: Put everything in a blender.
Blend until completely smooth.
Drink straight away.
tip: Use smooth nut butter only — crunchy has nut pieces. Look for jars that are just peanuts (and maybe salt).

title: Yoghurt with stewed pear
summary: Peeled pears gently cooked with cinnamon, spooned over thick yoghurt.
steps: Peel and core the pears, then cut into small pieces.
Put in a pan with the water, honey and cinnamon.
Cover and simmer gently for 8–10 minutes until very soft. Mash lightly if you like.
Spoon over the yoghurt, warm or cold.
tip: Peeling and cooking fruit removes the tough skin and softens the fibre.

title: Fluffy banana pancakes
summary: Simple homemade pancakes sweetened with ripe banana.
ingredients: Maple syrup and sliced banana, to serve
steps: Mash the banana in a bowl, then whisk in the eggs and milk.
Stir in the flour until just combined.
Heat a little butter in a non-stick pan over a medium heat.
Add small ladles of batter and cook for 2 minutes each side until golden.
Serve with maple syrup and banana.
tip: Homemade pancakes avoid the additives found in many shop-bought ones.

title: Mild shakshuka
summary: Eggs gently poached in a smooth, mildly spiced tomato and pepper sauce.
ingredients: 1 red pepper, peeled and finely chopped
steps: Peel the pepper with a vegetable peeler (or use jarred roasted peppers, which peel easily).
Fry the onion and pepper in the oil over a low heat for 10 minutes until very soft.
Add the cumin and paprika for 1 minute, then the passata. Simmer for 5 minutes.
Blend the sauce smooth with a stick blender if you like.
Make 4 hollows and crack in the eggs. Cover and cook for 6–8 minutes until the whites are set.
Crumble over the feta and serve with bread.
tip: Passata has no tomato skins or seeds, unlike tinned chopped tomatoes. Sweet paprika keeps it mild.

title: Cheese & spinach omelette
summary: A soft, folded omelette with wilted, finely chopped spinach and cheddar.
steps: Wilt the spinach in the pan with a splash of water, then chop it very finely.
Beat the eggs with salt and pepper.
Melt the butter in a non-stick pan, add the eggs and swirl.
When almost set, add the spinach and cheese to one half, fold over and cook for 1 more minute.
tip: Chopping cooked spinach finely breaks up the stringy leaves.

title: Carrot & ginger soup
summary: Bright, silky carrot soup with a gentle warmth from fresh ginger.
ingredients: Thumb-sized piece fresh ginger, peeled and grated
2 tbsp crème fraîche or a splash of milk
steps: Soften the onion in the oil for 5 minutes.
Add the carrots and ginger and cook for 2 minutes.
Pour in the stock, cover and simmer for 20 minutes until the carrots are very soft.
Blend until completely smooth, then stir in the crème fraîche.
tip: Blending makes soups one of the easiest ways to eat veg with strictures. Choose a stock with a short ingredient list, or make your own.

title: Butternut squash soup
summary: Velvety roasted squash soup — sweet, smooth and comforting.
ingredients: 1 butternut squash, peeled, deseeded and cubed
steps: Heat the oven to 200°C (180°C fan).
Toss the squash and onion in the oil and roast for 25 minutes until soft.
Tip into a pan with the stock and nutmeg and simmer for 5 minutes.
Blend until silky smooth. Stir in the cream if using.
tip: Make sure every squash seed is scooped out before roasting.

title: Red lentil & carrot soup
summary: A filling, protein-rich soup that blends to a smooth finish.
steps: Soften the onion and carrots in the oil for 5 minutes.
Stir in the cumin, then add the lentils and stock.
Simmer for 20 minutes until the lentils have fallen apart.
Blend smooth and add a squeeze of lemon.
tip: Red lentils are split and skinless, so they're much gentler than whole beans. Start with small portions if pulses are new to you.

title: Tomato soup & grilled cheese
summary: Smooth homemade tomato soup with a golden cheese toastie for dipping.
steps: Soften the onion in the butter for 8 minutes.
Add the passata, stock and sugar and simmer for 10 minutes.
Blend smooth and stir in the cream.
Butter the outside of the bread, fill with cheese and cook in a dry pan for 2–3 minutes each side until golden.
tip: Homemade soup avoids the thickeners and additives in many tinned soups.

title: Potato & leek soup
summary: A classic creamy soup, blended until totally smooth.
steps: Melt the butter and cook the leeks gently for 10 minutes until very soft.
Add the potatoes and stock and simmer for 15–20 minutes.
Add the milk and blend until completely smooth. Season to taste.
tip: Use only the pale part of the leek — the dark green tops are tougher and more fibrous.

title: Hummus & roast pepper wrap
summary: Soft tortilla with smooth hummus, peeled roast peppers and feta.
ingredients: 3 tbsp smooth hummus (see the homemade hummus recipe)
2 jarred roasted red peppers, skins removed
Few leaves of soft butter lettuce, finely shredded (optional)
steps: Warm the tortilla in a dry pan for a few seconds.
Spread with hummus.
Slice the peppers into strips, checking for any skin, and lay them on top.
Crumble over the feta, roll up tightly and cut in half.
tip: Leave out the lettuce on harder days. Jarred peppers are already cooked and peel easily.

title: Egg mayo sandwich
summary: Soft-boiled eggs mashed with mayo and chives on soft white bread.
steps: Boil the eggs for 9 minutes, then cool in cold water and peel.
Mash with the mayo, yoghurt, chives, salt and pepper.
Spread between the bread and cut into halves.
tip: Pick a mayonnaise with a short ingredient list, or mix half-and-half with yoghurt.

title: Courgette & feta fritters
summary: Golden fritters made with peeled, grated courgette and salty feta.
ingredients: Small handful of mint or dill, finely chopped
steps: Grate the peeled courgettes, then squeeze out as much water as you can in a clean tea towel.
Mix with the feta, eggs, flour and herbs.
Heat oil in a frying pan and add spoonfuls of the mix, flattening slightly.
Cook for 3 minutes each side until golden and cooked through. Serve with yoghurt.
tip: Peeling courgettes removes the tougher skin; the soft flesh is usually well tolerated when cooked.

title: Avocado & egg on toast
summary: Smashed avocado with a squeeze of lemon and a soft poached egg.
steps: Mash the avocado with the lemon, salt and pepper until smooth.
Poach the eggs in gently simmering water for 3 minutes.
Toast the bread, spread with avocado and top with the eggs.
tip: Skip chilli flakes and seeds that are often added to this dish.

title: Butternut squash dhal
summary: Mild, creamy red lentil dhal with soft squash and coconut milk.
ingredients: 300g butternut squash, peeled and diced small
steps: Soften the onion in the oil for 8 minutes, then add the garlic and spices for 1 minute.
Add the lentils, squash, coconut milk and stock.
Simmer for 25 minutes, stirring now and then, until the lentils are soft and the squash breaks up.
Mash or blend some of it for a smoother texture. Serve with rice.
tip: No chilli — the flavour comes from warming spices instead. White rice is lower in fibre than brown.

title: Butternut squash risotto
summary: Creamy risotto with soft roasted squash and parmesan-style cheese.
steps: Roast the squash in the oil at 200°C (180°C fan) for 25 minutes. Mash half of it.
Meanwhile, melt the butter and soften the onion for 5 minutes.
Stir in the rice for 1 minute, then add the stock a ladle at a time, stirring, for about 20 minutes.
Stir in the mashed squash, the cubes and the cheese. Rest for 2 minutes before serving.
tip: Traditional parmesan isn't vegetarian — look for a vegetarian hard cheese. Risotto rice is soft and low in fibre.

title: Lemon & spinach risotto
summary: Fresh, bright risotto with wilted spinach blended into the rice.
steps: Soften the onion in the butter for 5 minutes.
Add the rice and stir for 1 minute, then add the stock a ladle at a time, stirring, for 18–20 minutes.
Meanwhile, wilt the spinach and blend it with a splash of stock to a smooth purée.
Stir the spinach purée, lemon, cheese and mascarpone into the rice.
tip: Blending the spinach gives you the greens without the stringy leaves.

title: Butternut mac & cheese
summary: Homemade cheese sauce with puréed squash hidden inside.
steps: Boil the squash for 12 minutes until soft, then mash or blend smooth.
Cook the macaroni until soft. Drain.
Melt the butter, stir in the flour for 1 minute, then slowly whisk in the milk until thick.
Stir in the squash, most of the cheese, the mustard and nutmeg.
Mix with the pasta, top with the rest of the cheese and grill until bubbling.
tip: Cook pasta a little past al dente on harder days — softer pasta is easier to digest.

title: Sticky honey-soy tofu with rice
summary: Crispy tofu in a sticky, garlicky glaze with soft carrots and rice.
steps: Toss the tofu in the cornflour.
Fry in the oil for 8–10 minutes, turning, until golden.
Steam or boil the carrots for 8 minutes until very soft.
Mix the soy, honey, garlic and ginger, pour into the pan and bubble until sticky.
Serve over rice with the carrots.
tip: Leave off the sesame seeds that usually top this dish. Plain tofu is a minimally processed protein.

title: Mild butter paneer
summary: Paneer in a smooth, creamy tomato sauce — all flavour, no heat.
ingredients: White basmati rice or plain naan, to serve
steps: Fry the paneer in half the butter until golden. Set aside.
Melt the rest of the butter and soften the onion for 8 minutes. Add garlic, ginger and spices for 1 minute.
Add the passata and simmer for 10 minutes, then blend until smooth.
Stir in the cream, honey and paneer and heat through.
tip: Leave out chilli and fresh green chillies. Blending the sauce removes onion pieces.

title: Gnocchi & mozzarella bake
summary: Soft potato gnocchi baked in tomato sauce with melting mozzarella.
steps: Heat the oven to 200°C (180°C fan).
Warm the oil and garlic, add the passata and oregano and simmer for 10 minutes.
Boil the gnocchi for 2 minutes until they float. Drain and stir into the sauce.
Tip into a baking dish, top with mozzarella and bake for 15 minutes until bubbling.
tip: Choose gnocchi with a short ingredient list (mostly potato and flour), or make your own.

title: Lentil shepherd's pie
summary: Rich red lentil and carrot filling under fluffy, buttery mash.
ingredients: 1 tbsp vegetarian Worcestershire sauce or soy sauce
steps: Soften the onion and carrots in the oil for 10 minutes.
Add the lentils, tomato purée, Worcestershire, stock and thyme. Simmer for 20 minutes until thick.
Meanwhile, boil the potatoes until soft and mash with the butter and milk.
Spoon the filling into a dish, top with mash and cheese.
Bake at 200°C (180°C fan) for 20 minutes until golden.
tip: No peas here (a common stricture risk). Standard Worcestershire sauce contains anchovies — use a vegetarian one or soy.

title: Cauliflower cheese
summary: Tender cauliflower in a golden, bubbling cheddar sauce.
ingredients: 1 cauliflower, cut into small florets (stalks removed)
steps: Boil the florets for 8–10 minutes until very tender. Drain well.
Melt the butter, stir in the flour, then slowly whisk in the milk until thick.
Stir in most of the cheese and the mustard.
Pour over the cauliflower, top with the rest of the cheese and grill until golden.
tip: Use only the florets and cook them until very soft. Cauliflower can cause wind for some people, so try a small portion first.

title: Halloumi & peeled veg traybake
summary: Roasted sweet potato, carrots and courgette with golden halloumi.
ingredients: 3 carrots, peeled and cut into chunks
1 courgette, peeled and cut into chunks
steps: Heat the oven to 200°C (180°C fan).
Toss the veg with oil and oregano on a large tray and roast for 30 minutes.
Add the halloumi slices and roast for 10–15 minutes more until golden.
Finish with lemon.
tip: Roast until the veg is soft all the way through, not crunchy at the edges.

title: Simple egg fried rice
summary: Quick fried rice with egg and soft carrot — no peas or sweetcorn.
ingredients: 1 spring onion, green part only, finely sliced
steps: Heat the oil in a wok and cook the grated carrot for 2–3 minutes until soft.
Push to one side, add the eggs and scramble.
Add the rice and soy sauce and stir-fry until piping hot.
Scatter over the spring onion.
tip: Shop and takeaway versions usually include peas and sweetcorn — making it yourself avoids both.

title: Creamy roast pepper pasta
summary: Pasta in a silky blended sauce of roast peppers and cream cheese.
steps: Cook the pasta. Keep a cup of the water.
Blend the peppers, garlic, cream cheese and hard cheese until very smooth.
Warm the sauce in the pan, loosening with pasta water.
Toss with the pasta and top with basil.
tip: Blending the peppers removes any bits of skin.

title: Spinach & ricotta pasta bake
summary: Pasta shells baked with tomato sauce, creamy ricotta and blended spinach.
steps: Cook the pasta until soft. Drain.
Wilt the spinach, squeeze dry and blend or chop very finely. Mix with the ricotta, egg and nutmeg.
Warm the passata with the garlic for 5 minutes.
Mix the pasta with the sauce, dollop over the ricotta mix and top with mozzarella.
Bake at 200°C (180°C fan) for 20 minutes.
tip: Finely chopped or blended spinach is easier to digest than whole leaves.

title: Miso noodle soup with tofu
summary: A light, soothing broth with soft noodles and silken tofu.
ingredients: 1 carrot, peeled and cut into thin ribbons
1 spring onion, green part only, finely sliced
steps: Bring the water to a simmer with the ginger and carrot. Cook for 5 minutes.
Add the noodles and cook as the packet says.
Turn off the heat, then whisk in the miso and soy.
Add the tofu gently and serve topped with spring onion.
tip: Don't boil the miso — add it off the heat. Udon noodles are soft and low in fibre.

title: Mild sweet potato & coconut curry
summary: A gentle, creamy curry with peeled sweet potato and spinach.
steps: Soften the onion in the oil for 8 minutes. Add the garlic, ginger and curry powder for 1 minute.
Add the sweet potato, coconut milk and stock. Simmer for 20 minutes until soft.
Stir in the spinach until wilted.
Serve with rice.
tip: Pick a 'mild' curry powder and check it has no chilli listed high up.

title: Creamy baked eggs
summary: Eggs baked in little dishes with cream, spinach purée and cheese.
steps: Heat the oven to 180°C (160°C fan). Butter 2 ramekins.
Divide the spinach between them, crack 2 eggs into each and spoon over the cream.
Top with cheese and bake for 12–15 minutes until the whites are set.
Serve with toast for dipping.
tip: A quick, soft, high-protein meal for days when you don't feel like much.

title: Cheesy polenta with tomato sauce
summary: Soft, creamy polenta topped with a slow-simmered smooth tomato sauce.
steps: Warm the oil and garlic, add the passata and simmer for 15 minutes.
Bring the stock to the boil and whisk in the polenta. Cook, stirring, for 5 minutes until thick.
Beat in the butter and cheese.
Spoon into bowls and top with the sauce and basil.
tip: Polenta is made from finely ground corn, without the tough husks of whole sweetcorn kernels. Try a small portion first.

title: Stewed apple & custard
summary: Soft cinnamon apple with simple homemade custard.
steps: Simmer the apples, sugar, cinnamon and water with a lid on for 10 minutes until soft.
For the custard, heat the milk until steaming.
Whisk the yolks, sugar, cornflour and vanilla, then slowly whisk in the hot milk.
Return to the pan and stir over a low heat until thick. Pour over the apples.
tip: Homemade custard avoids colourings and thickeners in many ready-made versions.

title: Creamy rice pudding
summary: Slow-cooked pudding rice in vanilla milk — pure comfort.
steps: Put the rice, milk, sugar and vanilla in a pan.
Simmer very gently for 30–35 minutes, stirring often, until thick and creamy.
Stir in the butter and top with nutmeg.
tip: Very gentle and filling — a good choice during a flare.

title: Simple banana bread
summary: Moist, nut-free banana bread with a short, simple ingredient list.
steps: Heat the oven to 180°C (160°C fan) and line a loaf tin.
Mash the bananas, then stir in the butter, sugar, egg and vanilla.
Fold in the bicarb, salt and flour.
Pour into the tin and bake for 50–60 minutes until a skewer comes out clean.
tip: No walnuts or seeds — just plain banana bread.

title: Silky homemade hummus
summary: Extra-smooth hummus with warm pitta for dipping.
steps: For the smoothest hummus, pinch the skins off the chickpeas (or simmer them for 10 minutes with ½ tsp bicarb, then rinse).
Blend the tahini and lemon first until creamy.
Add the chickpeas, garlic and oil, and blend for 3–4 minutes, adding water until silky.
Serve with warm pitta.
tip: Removing the chickpea skins and blending for longer gives a much smoother result. Tahini is smooth ground sesame, not whole seeds.
